# Architecture

The extension has four independent parts: audio ownership, compact musical features, declarative spatial worlds, and glyph rendering.

**Audio ownership.** The MV3 action receives the intended source tab before creating or focusing the visualizer. The service worker serializes capture mutations, stores only session capture identity, and creates one USER_MEDIA offscreen document. That document consumes a short-lived tab stream ID, connects the stereo source directly to the audio destination exactly once, and sends timestamped compact features at 30 Hz. Analysers use a separate unity-gain branch, including explicit stereo upmix for mono inputs. No raw PCM crosses extension messages. Stop, source termination and visualizer-tab removal close tracks, contexts and the offscreen document. File and display-sharing routes use the same AudioOwner in the visible page.

**Musical features.** A 2048-sample stereo FFT supplies broad band energy and spectral change; time-domain samples supply level and stereo imbalance. Bounded reference normalization, a noise gate, separate attack/release time constants, a slow activity envelope, and conservative onset/interval confidence prevent silence from becoming frantic movement. Band labels describe frequencies, not inferred instruments. Renderer sensitivity never changes the audio playback connection. Rhythm estimates refine scene boundaries only when confidence is adequate.

**Spatial worlds.** Thirty-two locally bundled analytic constructions feed independent layers. A layer can wrap, repel, weave, intersect, or gradually blend another construction, and can fold, twist, ripple, split, grow, circulate, invert, or collapse. Authored rows specify these relationships, placement roles, openings, cameras and musical mappings explicitly. Discovery changes graph structure, construction choices, layer count, containment/crossing/constellation/corridor arrangement, apertures and mappings. It validates numeric bounds, extent, projected visibility, approximate negative space and recent structural fingerprints, with at most twelve candidate attempts and an identified authored fallback. No executable presets, eval, external model, downloaded operators or unrestricted code synthesis are involved.

The operator called `tesseract` constructs nested cubic edge cages; it does not claim an exact four-dimensional projection. `reaction` constructs nonlinear interference patterns; it is not a reaction-diffusion PDE solver. Parametric constructions are selected for their visible behavior and bounded cost, rather than mathematical branding.

**Glyph fabric.** Stable low-discrepancy sample identities occupy the constructions directly. GPU transform feedback calculates positions, local projected tangents, normals and color once per mark at a maximum of 30 updates per second. It also retains each mark’s categorical glyph ID and last form-change time. Drawing reuses this buffer through instanced bitmap quads. Perspective, depth-buffered opaque mask pixels and porous openings establish real near/far relationships without a mesh rasterization step.

ANSI Tube’s coverage, centroid, occupancy and directional descriptors score analytic local band/half-plane targets against the exact 32 canonical masks. A cached structural lookup gives candidates; persistent score bias and minimum dwell create hysteresis. Form choice responds to projected structure and the layer’s musical articulation. It is never an index-based morph or random per-frame character assignment.

**Palette preparation.** A local worker prepares exact source palette colors, the source 5-bit finite lookup and exact 256-step styled luminance ramps away from playback. The GPU applies source brightness/saturation grading first, then the style treatment, then finite quantization. True Color bypasses finite quantization and retains 8-bit RGB output. Shader floating-point rounding is checked against the original CPU functions and its tolerance is documented in the verification report. Changing a palette invalidates cached mark colors before the first new draw. The retained bundle cache has an eight-entry bound. Binary atlas sampling, no blending or multisampling, disabled dithering and nearest-neighbor display keep finite output testable. All normal readbacks are confined to development diagnostics and verification.

**Playback and retention.** The scheduler accounts visible automatic seconds, corrects the authored-time deficit probabilistically, limits streaks, and never resets the authored queue when Discovery runs. Upcoming scenes are bounded data objects rather than a second renderer. Glyph presence creates compatible entrances/exits without doubling GPU scene cost. Forty recent worlds, up to one hundred saved Discoveries and bounded favorites/preferences persist locally. Imported data is normalized through schema version 1 and operator/generator version 1.0.0.

Quality changes mark sampling, draw cadence and internal resolution while retaining the selected alphabet, palette and color depth. Each scene’s base sampling budget limits the quality budget before the user’s bounded density multiplier; there are at most 8,000 samples per layer and five layers. Simulated features remain clearly labeled. The application is a dependency-free ES-module project; Playwright and Sharp are development verification tools, not extension runtime dependencies.
